title: Sharad Navratri: The Complete 9-Day Guide
introText: {"type":"doc","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","marks":[{"type":"italic"}],"text":"Ghatasthapana to Maha Navami — nine forms, nine nights, one Mother"}]}]}
sankalpaBody: I will observe the nine nights of Navratri with a clean mind and body, worshiping the nine forms of Durga, to attain strength, peace, and spiritual growth.
sankalpaQuote: Mamabhipretha siddhyartham shri devata aradhanatam sankalpam karishye.
fastOptions: [{"name":"Full Nine-Day Fast","desc":"No grains, sendha namak only, phalahar through the day.","recommended":true},{"name":"Partial Fast","desc":"Observe fast on Pratipada, Ashtami, and Navami only.","recommended":false},{"name":"First and Last","desc":"Observe fast on Day 1 and Day 9 only.","recommended":false}]
fastNote: The tradition prescribes devotion, not starvation. If a nine-day fast is not physically possible for you, a shorter form kept with sincerity fulfils the vrat.
kathaTitle: The story the nine nights re-enact
kathaBody: {"type":"doc","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Devi Mahatmya tells it plainly. The gods were losing. Mahishasura had taken heaven and no god could defeat him. The collective energy of all the gods converged into one form: Durga. She fought for nine nights, and on the tenth day she won."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Every year the tradition re-enacts that arc, not as mythology but as practice. You set up a kalash. You light a flame and keep it lit. You worship a different form of the Mother each day. And on the tenth day you mark the outcome."}]}]}

panchangNote: Saptami covers both 17 and 18 October this year, so the observance stretches across ten civil days. Panchangs differ on whether Durga Ashtami falls on 18 or 19 October — see the Panchang article. Follow your family or community panchang.

steps.title: Clean the space
steps.description: Clean the space. Place a chowki and cover it with red cloth.

steps.title: Kalash sthapana
steps.description: Fill a brass or copper kalash with water, add akshat, a coin and a supari, place five or seven mango leaves around the rim, seal with a coconut.

steps.title: Sow barley or sapta-dhanya
steps.description: Sow barley or sapta-dhanya in a small clay pot of soil. Water lightly.

steps.title: Install Durga image
steps.description: Place the Durga image or idol behind the kalash and install it with prayer.

steps.title: Light the akhand jyoti
steps.description: Light the akhand jyoti — a ghee lamp intended to burn through the nine days. Use a vessel large enough to hold sufficient ghee or oil.

steps.title: Offer flowers and prayers
steps.description: Offer flowers, incense and fruit. Chant Ya Devi Sarvabhuteshu, or Durga Saptashati Chapter 1.

mantras.meaning: Salutations to Maa Kalaratri, the dark destroyer of ignorance.
Salutations to Maa Mahagauri, the radiant mother of purity.
Salutations to Maa Siddhidatri, the bestower of all supernatural powers.
Salutations to Maa Shailaputri, the daughter of the mountain.
Salutations to Maa Brahmacharini, the one who practices severe penance.
Salutations to Maa Chandraghanta, the one who wears a crescent moon.
Salutations to Maa Kushmanda, the creator of the universe.
Salutations to Maa Skandamata, the mother of Lord Skanda.
Salutations to Maa Katyayani, the fierce warrior goddess.

dpbEntries.elementName: Durga worship across Ashwin Shukla Paksha
dpbEntries.claim: Worship of Durga across the nine nights of Ashwin Shukla Paksha
dpbEntries.sourceOfTruth: Devi Mahatmya, Markandeya Purana. THIS IS THE CORE CLAIM.

dpbEntries.elementName: Navadurga — nine forms across nine days
dpbEntries.claim: Navadurga — nine forms across nine days

dpbEntries.sourceOfTruth: Prescribed across Shakta tradition; Agama puja procedure.
Worship of girls as living forms of the Devi; attested in Shakta tradition.

dpbEntries.claim: Sowing barley on the first day is a widespread North Indian practice rather than a scriptural requirement. Where it is kept, the sprouts are watched through the nine days and distributed as prasad at the end.
dpbEntries.sourceOfTruth: Popular, varies by year and by source. No named text.
Gujarat cultural celebration. Not a Puranic prescription.
Widespread North Indian practice. No named text.

dpbEntries.elementName: “If the Akhand Jyoti goes out, Navratri is wasted”
dpbEntries.claim: If the Akhand Jyoti goes out, the whole Navratri is wasted.
dpbEntries.correction: Relight it and continue. The tradition values the intention of maintaining a continuous flame. An accidental extinguishing does not cancel the days already kept. This fear contradicts the Devi’s own teaching — she fights for you, not against you.

dpbEntries.elementName: “The wrong colour on a day brings bad luck”
dpbEntries.claim: Wearing the wrong colour on a day brings bad luck.
dpbEntries.correction: The daily colour system is custom, not scripture. No named text assigns colours to days. If you wear green on a red day, nothing is owed and nothing is lost.

dpbEntries.elementName: “Kanya Pujan must be exactly nine girls”
dpbEntries.claim: Kanya Pujan must be exactly nine girls — fewer is disrespectful.
dpbEntries.correction: Nine is the ideal, matching the nine forms. Two, five and seven are all accepted across traditions. The practice is the honouring, not the headcount.

introDesc: Navratri means nine nights. It is not nine separate festivals — it is one continuous arc of worship, moving from darkness through fire to light.

kathaCardHeadline: The gods were losing, and no god could win
heroImageCaption: Day 1. The kalash is filled. The barley is sown. The flame begins. Nine nights start here.
sankalpaSub: Said once, at the start, before anything else is done.
sankalpaDesc: A sankalpa is a stated intention, not a formula that must be pronounced correctly. It names who is doing it, when, where and for what. That is the whole of its structure.
vidhiSubtitle: Sunday 11 October · Maa Shailputri, daughter of the mountain — Parvati in her first form.
vidhiMuhuratNote: Muhurat. Morning 6:19–10:12 AM is preferred. Abhijit muhurat, 11:44 AM–12:31 PM, is the fallback. Ghatasthapana is not performed after midday.
kathaCardTeaser: Mahishasura had taken heaven. What defeated him was not a stronger god — it was every god surrendering their power into one form.
kathaWhyNineNightsNote: the battle took nine. The reading follows the fight rather than summarising it.

kathaSteps.title: The boon
kathaSteps.description: Mahishasura cannot be killed by any man or god. He asks for the exemption he thinks is safest.

kathaSteps.title: Heaven falls
kathaSteps.description: The devas are driven out. Each one alone is not enough, and they know it.

kathaSteps.title: The convergence
kathaSteps.description: Their combined energy takes one form — Durga, holding a weapon from each of them.

kathaSteps.title: Nine nights
kathaSteps.description: She fights for nine nights. On the tenth day, she wins.

deepDiveTeaser: Nine nights appear across the tradition — four Navratris in a year, not one. The count, the arc from tamas through rajas to sattva, and why the tenth day sits outside the nine are explained once and apply to all of them.
deepDiveClosingText:
Navratri is the tradition's most sustained worship — nine nights without a break. The kalash stays filled. The flame stays lit. The flowers are replaced each morning. The mantra changes daily.

And on the ninth night you look at the barley you sowed on the first day, now tall and green and reaching upward, and you understand what the nine nights were doing: growing something that was barely a seed when you began.
